content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text resolves a chain-versus-link dispute by adverting to chapter-bound verses and a word-count rather than weighing the pressed witnesses as a chain against the link's chain by footing.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: (1) the judge must assess the pressed witnesses together as a chain and compare its overall footing with the link's chain; (2) the judge may test the verses or word-counts individually so long as no single verse states the contrary.", "why": "It treats the Isaiah chapter bounds and the almah/bethulah word-count as separate verse-level counters and labels the issue underdetermined, instead of weighing the pressed chain against the link's chain by footing as K-C requires."}
